items.question: What is meant by the term cosmic egg in this context?
premises: The mass turns toward manifestation.
It emerges from the form of power.
It is free from placing and removing.
items.inference: Therefore this unified mass of reality is called the cosmic egg.
uncertainties: āvāpavāna may refer to technical ritual placement and removal or to general addition and subtraction.
items.plain_english: The cosmic egg is the mass of reality that has turned toward manifestation, emerged from the form of power, and remains undivided by any placing or removing.

rows.grounds: identifies the upper shell with sattva
identifies the lower shell with sattva

items.question: How are the upper and lower shells of the cosmic egg described?
premises: The upper shell is sattva touched by a trace of darkness.
The lower shell is sattva touched by passion.
The lower aspect is also associated with darkness.
items.inference: Thus the two shells of the egg are differentiated by mixtures of the three qualities.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of nirmṛṣṭaṃ sattvam to the lower shell is compressed.
items.plain_english: The upper shell of the egg is purity touched by a trace of darkness, while the lower shell is purity touched by passion and associated with darkness.

rows.grounds: explains the nature of the mass

items.question: Why is the mass of reality said to become the cosmic egg?
premises: The mass of reality partakes of the aggregate of Shiva and Shakti.
In its manifestation there is a turning toward.
This turning toward is what is being defined.
items.inference: Therefore the mass of reality is called the egg because of its oriented manifestation.
uncertainties: The boundary between the two quoted definitions in the verse is interpretive.
items.plain_english: The mass of reality is said to partake of the aggregate of Shiva and Shakti, and when it turns toward manifestation it is called the cosmic egg.

rows.grounds: states why they are not eggs

items.question: Why do powers immersed in Shiva not become cosmic eggs?
premises: An objection arises that powers immersed in Shiva might become eggs.
Another clarifying statement is given for this case.
Those powers have not fallen from their state as power.
items.inference: Therefore powers immersed in Shiva do not become eggs because they do not fall from power-ness.
uncertainties: The exact referent of vākyamaparaṃ is the phrase in the next verse.
items.plain_english: One might object that powers immersed in Shiva would also become eggs, but they do not, because they have not fallen from their nature as power.

rows.grounds: states the doubt to be avoided

items.question: Why should egg-ness not be suspected in bodies and other elements?
premises: A doubt may arise about egg-ness in bodies and other elements.
Another clarifying word addresses this doubt.
In those elements there is no placing of anything.
items.inference: Therefore egg-ness should not be suspected in bodies and other elements.
uncertainties: tanvakṣa is taken as body and related constituents; the exact technical scope is compressed.
items.plain_english: One should not suspect egg-ness in bodies and similar elements, because in them there is no placing or removing of anything.

items.question: How can a collection of bodies and elements be one?
premises: A collection of bodies and elements raises the question of oneness.
The term undivided is applied to that collection.
That term shows sameness of kind.
items.inference: Therefore the collection can be called one because its members share the same kind.
uncertainties: The verse compresses the referent of the quoted term anirbhakta.
items.plain_english: If bodies and elements form a collection, their oneness is explained by calling them undivided, which indicates that they are of the same kind.

items.question: Why would egg-nature not apply to every principle individually?
premises: Even without the term mass of reality, egg-nature might seem possible in the principles.
An objection asks why that would not be so.
The verse sets up a restriction on the term's application.
items.inference: Therefore egg-nature does not automatically apply to each principle taken separately.
uncertainties: The verse is transitional and its full answer comes in the next verses.
items.plain_english: Even without using the term mass of reality, one might think each principle could be an egg by nature; but the text raises the question of why that is not the case.

items.question: What does the word reality mean in the definition of the egg?
premises: If egg-nature applied too broadly, it would follow even in a principle made of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements.
The answer turns on the meaning of the word reality.
That word refers to what consists of body, elements, and worlds.
items.inference: Therefore the word reality restricts egg-nature to the structured totality of body, elements, and worlds.
uncertainties: tanvakṣa is interpreted broadly as body and related constituents.
items.plain_english: If egg-nature were taken too broadly, it would apply even to a principle made only of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements; but the word reality here means what consists of body, elements, and worlds.

rows.grounds: grounds the aggregate in the lord

items.question: Why is the aggregate of that form called the cosmic egg?
premises: The relevant form has already been stated.
The aggregate of that form is called the egg.
That aggregate belongs to the lord who bears the universal body.
items.inference: Therefore the cosmic egg is the aggregate of that defined form as held within the lord's universal body.
uncertainties: The verse leaves implicit how the lord's universal body relates to each egg.
items.plain_english: Because that form has already been defined, its aggregate is called the cosmic egg; and that aggregate can be understood as belonging to the lord who bears the universal body.

items.question: Why were additional distinguishing terms introduced for the path-sphere?
premises: Additional distinguishing terms were taken up for this purpose.
The discussion concerns states of only that limited extent.
Those states occur in the path-sphere dependent on maya.
items.inference: Therefore extra distinguishing terms were needed to prevent confusion in the maya-dependent path-sphere.
uncertainties: The exact set of bhedaka terms is not enumerated in this verse.
items.plain_english: For that reason, other distinguishing terms were introduced, so that in the limited states of the path-sphere dependent on maya there would be no confusion.

rows.grounds: introduces the reason for the next verse

items.question: What cosmological fact follows after the Brahma egg has been described?
premises: Others explain the distinguishing terms as preventing egg-ness in the wrong cases.
The Brahma egg has already been described.
Beyond that egg there are one hundred Rudras.
items.inference: Therefore the text now turns from the Brahma egg to the hundred Rudras beyond it.
uncertainties: The verse functions as a bridge, so its full sense depends on verse 180.
items.plain_english: Others say the distinguishing terms were used to prevent egg-ness from being wrongly applied; and once the Brahma egg has been described, the text notes that beyond it there are one hundred Rudras.

items.question: Who are the lords of the hundred Rudras beyond the Brahma egg?
premises: The hundred Rudras have their own lords.
Those lords are eleven Rudras of great radiance.
The verse begins naming them as Ananta, Kapalin, Agni, Yama, Nairrita, and Bala.
items.inference: Therefore the hundred Rudras are ruled by eleven radiant Rudra-lords beginning with Ananta.
uncertainties: The full list of eleven names continues into verse 181.
items.plain_english: The hundred Rudras beyond the Brahma egg have eleven radiant Rudra-lords of their own, beginning with Ananta, Kapalin, Agni, Yama, Nairrita, and Bala.

items.question: How is the surrounding presence of the Rudra-lords illustrated?
premises: The list of eleven Rudra-lords continues with Shighra, Nidhisha, Vidyesha, Shambhu, and Virabhadra.
A simile compares their surrounding action to bees.
Bees cover nectar, kadamba flowers, and clusters of filaments.
items.inference: Therefore the Rudra-lords are pictured as surrounding their domain like bees covering flowers.
uncertainties: The exact objects covered in the simile are compressed into a poetic list.
items.plain_english: The remaining Rudra-lords are Shighra, Nidhisha, Vidyesha, Shambhu, and Virabhadra; and they are likened to bees covering nectar, kadamba flowers, and filaments.

items.question: How many Shiva-Rudras surround the Brahma egg and how are they arranged?
premises: The simile of covering is applied to the Shiva-Rudras.
They surround the Brahma egg with countless retinues.
Their arrangement is counted as five times eight niyutas, that is, a koti.
items.inference: Therefore a vast host of Shiva-Rudras, numbering a koti, surrounds the Brahma egg.
uncertainties: The exact numerical parsing of śarāṣṭaniyutaṃ depends on traditional number terms.
items.plain_english: In the same way, the Shiva-Rudras with countless retinues surround the Brahma egg; their arrangement is said to number a koti, described as five times eight niyutas.

items.question: What role do the Shiva-Rudras play under Shrikantha according to the Raurava commentary?
premises: The Shiva-Rudras are presided over by Shrikantha.
They create and withdraw.
They hold lordship over the gods according to the Raurava commentary.
items.inference: Therefore, under Shrikantha, the Shiva-Rudras exercise cosmic creation, withdrawal, and lordship over the gods.
uncertainties: The exact scope of diviṣadām could mean gods in general or a specific class.
items.plain_english: According to the Raurava commentary, these Shiva-Rudras are presided over by Shrikantha; they create and withdraw, and they exercise lordship over the gods.

items.question: What alternative cosmology does the Siddha Tantra give beyond the golden egg?
premises: The Siddha Tantra gives a different account.
Beyond a hundred kotis from the golden egg there are one hundred eggs.
These eggs appear in sequence, doubled again and again, and joined with silver and other materials.
items.inference: Therefore the Siddha Tantra describes a further series of one hundred material eggs beyond the golden egg.
uncertainties: The precise meaning of dvidviguṇaṃ in this cosmological sequence is compressed.
items.plain_english: But in the Siddha Tantra, beyond a hundred kotis from the golden egg, there is a sequence of one hundred further eggs, progressively doubled and made of silver and other materials.

items.question: What happens in the sequence of eggs described by the Siddha Tantra?
premises: In those eggs there are Brahmas in sequence.
Their lifespans are doubled in that sequence.
They diminish in order, and at the end comes the water principle.
items.inference: Therefore the series of eggs contains Brahmas of increasing lifespan who decline in order until the water principle is reached.
uncertainties: ammayam is read as made of water; the compound is terse.
items.plain_english: In those eggs, Brahmas appear in sequence with doubled lifespans; they diminish in order, and at the end of that series comes the principle made of water.

items.question: How do the principles expand in measure from earth upward in this account?
premises: From earth upward come water and the other principles in order.
The expansion is tenfold up to ego.
Beyond that, intellect is a hundredfold.
items.inference: Therefore the path of principles expands by increasing multiples from earth up through ego and intellect.
uncertainties: The verse gives ratios but not the base unit of measurement.
items.plain_english: From earth upward, water and the other principles follow in order; the expansion is tenfold up to ego, and beyond that intellect is a hundredfold.

rows.grounds: names the next principle and measure

items.question: What measures are assigned to the principles above intellect in this sequence?
premises: Manifest nature is a thousandfold beyond intellect.
The masculine principle is ten thousandfold.
Niyati is a hundred thousandfold and beyond that comes a millionfold.
items.inference: Therefore the higher principles continue the sequence with rapidly increasing multiples.
uncertainties: The verse leaves the millionfold referent to be completed in verse 188.
items.plain_english: Beyond intellect, manifest nature is a thousandfold, the masculine principle is ten thousandfold, niyati is a hundred thousandfold, and beyond that the measure becomes a millionfold.

rows.grounds: names the next principle and measure

items.question: How far does the ascending scale of measures extend up to Sadakhya?
premises: Up to kala the measure is ten millionfold.
From that come maya and knowledge at a hundred millionfold.
Ishvara is a billionfold and beyond that comes a thousand kotis fold.
items.inference: Therefore the scale continues expanding through kala, maya, knowledge, and Ishvara toward Sadakhya.
uncertainties: The exact attachment of viddaśakoṭidhā to maya or knowledge is compressed in the compound.
items.plain_english: Up to kala the measure is ten millionfold; beyond that come maya and knowledge at a hundred millionfold, Ishvara at a billionfold, and then a thousand kotis fold leading onward.

items.question: How does Sadakhya relate to the all-pervading goddess and the entire path?
premises: Sadakhya pervades at the top of the measured sequence.
It does so together with a multitude of powers.
The all-pervading goddess stands established having pervaded the entire path.
items.inference: Therefore Sadakhya and the goddess together pervade the entire path.
uncertainties: The relation between Sadakhya and the goddess is close but not fully specified syntactically.
items.plain_english: Sadakhya pervades, together with a multitude of powers, and the all-pervading goddess stands established as having pervaded the entire path.

items.question: What is said about the supreme Shiva principle beyond all measure?
premises: Beyond the measured sequence is the pure, supreme Shiva principle.
It is known as immeasurable.
From water onward up to the Shiva principle, none but Shiva has seen it.
items.inference: Therefore the supreme Shiva principle transcends the measurable path and is fully known only by Shiva.
uncertainties: The scope of what is not seen by anyone but Shiva is stated broadly and may include the whole range.
items.plain_english: Beyond all that is the pure, supreme, immeasurable Shiva principle; from water onward up to that principle, no one but Shiva has truly seen it.

items.question: What is presented as the supreme cause of liberation after the account of the path?
premises: Only Shiva fully knows the highest principle.
Therefore knowledge of Shiva is supreme.
Mahadeva states this in the revered Svacchanda scripture.
items.inference: Therefore supreme knowledge of Shiva is the cause of liberation.
uncertainties: The verse introduces the citation whose content follows in verse 192.
items.plain_english: Therefore, supreme knowledge of Shiva is the cause of liberation, as Mahadeva declares in the revered Svacchanda scripture.

items.question: Why is Shaiva initiation necessary for liberation according to this citation?
premises: A bound soul does not attain liberation by hundreds of other knowledges.
Knowledge of Shiva does not arise without Shaiva initiation.
The citation presents this as an exclusive condition.
items.inference: Therefore Shaiva initiation is necessary because it is the condition for the arising of liberating knowledge of Shiva.
uncertainties: jñānaśatairapi is rhetorical and not meant as a literal count.
items.plain_english: A bound soul does not attain liberation by hundreds of other kinds of knowledge; knowledge of Shiva does not arise without receiving Shaiva initiation.
